WHY ROW 1'S LITERAL IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN THE PRE-REGISTERED EXAMPLE, AND WHY IT IS ALSO THE RIGHT-EDGE ANCHOR - the two requirements the limb imposes, which had to be satisfied at once. That adjacency exists only where the register's own cells are contiguous in the tag-stripped stream, so a title, a link label or a 'recently added' panel cannot reproduce it, which is the entire purpose of the boundary rule (2026-09-24, class (A') converted from a post-hoc judgement into a precondition). (b) RIGHT-EDGE ANCHORED: the literal begins 29 characters behind 'Petaquilla Minerals Ltd. v. R', where this project's observation of the register ends, so approximately 371 of the 400 excerpt characters (EXCERPT_CHARS = 400, scripts/fetch_relay.py:41) fall on register this council has never observed. R' would anchor at the edge but span no boundary and would therefore NOT discharge the limb; a bare 'ARB/25/26' would span no boundary either and is the exact form the limb's own words exclude.

'Manifest Lack of Legal Merit' is 11 fired / 11 TRUE on this URL, every one ok/200 - the strongest attested control this council holds on this surface.

THE CONTROL LADDER, AND WHY THREE ROWS RATHER THAN ONE. Row 1 can legitimately null, and excerpt_of returns the EMPTY STRING on a miss (scripts/fetch_relay.py:132-133) rather than a head excerpt, so a null row hands back no window at all and cannot by itself show that the tag-strip yielded any prose from that byte stream. Per analytics/fetch-requests/README.md every URL expected to be capable of a null needs a same-run companion on the same URL. Rows sharing a URL with different find values are separate fetches and cost one slot each. The three rows are a LADDER, and each rung isolates a different failure: row 3 ('Manifest Lack of Legal Merit', 11/11 TRUE) establishes that the ORIGIN ANSWERED and the tag-strip yielded page prose, independent of the register's state; row 2 ('ARB/25/26) Decision', cell-spanning) establishes that the REGISTER TABLE ITSELF was reached and that the Karapetyan entry still renders with its designation cell contiguous; row 1 establishes whether THE EDGE IS STILL WHERE WE LEFT IT. Read them in the order 3, 2, 1. A FALSE on row 3 voids the reading of any null above it. A TRUE on row 3 with a FALSE on row 2 is an OBSERVATION THAT THE REGISTER MOVED - it is NOT a statement that the Karapetyan entry was removed, because the find is exact as to form and a re-render of that one cell would break the literal while leaving the entry in place. A TRUE on row 2 with a FALSE on row 1 locates the change between the Karapetyan and E.ON entries and is likewise an instrument observation, never a statement about what ICSID published or withdrew.

WHAT A TRUE ON ROW 1 WOULD AND WOULD NOT FOUND, FIXED HERE BEFORE THE ROWS FIRE. IT WOULD FOUND: the party names, case designators, document designations and dates that ICSID itself renders in that region of that register at the batch instant, as rendered. IT WOULD NOT FOUND: any disposition, holding, ground or outcome. G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition and G10 bars reading a document designation as a tribunal's characterisation. In particular NO ROW BELOW CAN CLOSE THREAD 11, whose closure condition requires the BODY of a primary document stating that the ground was whether an IP right is a covered investment; and no row below can open thread 11's third 'gate fired / IP asserted / non-IP ground' bucket, which also requires an indication that IP was asserted. The POST-HOC BACKSTOP TEST still applies to whatever window returns, per 2026-09-24: at least two complete register triples for DIFFERENT cases, the find literal sitting inside or adjacent to a case-number parenthetical, and a terminating boundary on one side.

ABSENCE DISCIPLINE, CARRIED AND NOT RE-LITIGATED. Anything not in a returned 400-character window is 'not found in the region observed', NEVER 'the register contains no such matter' - the 2026-08-20 absence limb was dropped on 2026-09-24 precisely because absence from a 400-character window is not absence from a ~96-kilobyte page, and this council has never read that page. A party-name register carries party names and not subjects, so no row below can found a statement that no IP, trade-secret, pharmaceutical or clinical-data matter appears on this register.

That row was queued by the chairman on 2026-10-01 to 'the cadenced batch on or about 2026-10-13' - this batch - on the stated ground that 'analytics/locked_set/VALIDATION_RECORD.md row 1-03 already identifies pca-cpa.org as a locator for this caption'. THAT GROUND IS FALSE, verified by execution at session head: VALIDATION_RECORD.md:290 row 1-03 is 'Merck & Co., Inc. v. Republic of Ecuador', PCA Case No. 2012-10 - a DIFFERENT MATTER. The Servier row is 1-02 at :289 and its candidate locator is 'italaw.com - case page for this caption (numeric case id not verified)', and www.italaw.com and bare italaw.com are under this council's standing fetch prohibition. A grep for 'pca-cpa' across every .md, .json and .jsonl in the repository returns NO pca-cpa.org locator tied to the Servier caption anywhere. So no PCA case id for this matter is held, PCA case pages are addressed as /en/cases/<numeric id>/ (4 ids attested: 309, 336, 50, and the news path), and firing a PCA index or search surface to find one would be a DISCOVERY use, which scripts/fetch_relay.py's own header forbids and which the research analyst correctly declined on exactly this reasoning on 2026-10-12 for the Philip Morris Asia docket. Recovering the numeric id is operator-side or search-side work.
